I'm exploring how to compress diagonals in a grid. I have an input pattern with specific points around the center and need to output a 3x3 matrix that reflects key values. I see nonzero elements at corners and edges, plus a center point, which will guide my extraction of rows and columns. I need to be careful about mapping these elements accurately while considering that I might need to remove any zero rows or columns along the way. It's a bit tricky!

**Analyzing diagonal patterns**

I'm working through the idea of reading diagonal cross patterns, where my output rows correspond to the NW-SE diagonal lines. I think the output array will organize values based on coordinates from symmetric axes. This means I'll be compressing dimensions by pairing diagonally, drawing from input coordinates where the row and column add up. I need to test this approach and perhaps write a program to demonstrate and map these values accurately before submitting my findings. It's a bit of a puzzle!
